_meta.asset: Golden corpus - the AT's OWN worked examples
_meta.why_this_matters: These four payloads are transcribed verbatim from section 5 of the AT's QR specification. They were written by the tax authority, not by the author of this engine. That makes them a genuinely INDEPENDENT oracle: if the reconciliation logic here is wrong, these fail, and no amount of internally-consistent hand-derived test data can paper over it. A sibling project (AoCentimo) shipped a corpus that was entirely self-derived and was consequently blind to a wrong constant for a year; this corpus exists so that failure mode is not repeated.
_meta.source: Especificacoes Tecnicas Codigo de Barras Bidimensional (Codigo QR), AT, seccao 5, exemplos 1-4
_meta.transcription: Payload strings copied character-for-character from the specification. Do NOT 'tidy' them.

cases.label: Exemplo 1 - Fatura spanning continente + Acores + Madeira, com imposto do selo e retencao
cases.why_included: The only fixture that exercises J*, K*, L and M together. An engine that ignores any of those still reconciles the simple cases and fails here.

cases.label: Exemplo 2 - Fatura simplificada, 0.80 EUR (a coffee)
cases.why_included: Cent-scale amounts, and the single most common real-world receipt shape: a till slip with no NIF, where the deduction is simply lost.

cases.label: Exemplo 3 - Fatura pro-forma (NOT a purchase)
cases.why_included: A pro-forma arithmetically reconciles perfectly and is NOT a purchase. Nothing may be deducted and no guarantee period starts. An engine that trusts arithmetic alone will happily produce both.

cases.label: Exemplo 4 - Documento de transporte, sem valores, I1:0
cases.why_included: Legitimately carries no amounts at all and sets I1:0. A naive 'no breakdown means something is wrong' rule fires falsely here, so the engine must distinguish 'no amounts because this is not a valued document' from 'no amounts because the read failed'.
